unit.title: Weather, Travel and the World Around Us

theory.title: Describing landscapes and choosing outdoor activities
theory.explanation: Use comparative adjectives to compare places: A lake is quieter than a beach. Use the + superlative to identify the top example: This is the highest mountain. Use should/shouldn't to give advice: You should wear walking boots. Use must/mustn't for important rules: Visitors mustn't leave rubbish. Use can/can't for possibility and permission.
theory.tip: Short adjectives often add -er/-est (high, higher, the highest). Longer adjectives use more/most (more beautiful, the most beautiful). Use than after a comparative.

patterns.label: Block 1 · Comparatives · short adjectives
examples: The lake is quieter than the beach.
This path is longer than that one.

patterns.label: Block 2 · Comparatives · spelling
examples: The hill is bigger than the field.
This route is safer than the old one.

patterns.label: Block 3 · Comparatives · long adjectives
examples: The forest is more beautiful than the town.
Cycling is more exciting than walking.

patterns.label: Block 4 · Superlatives · short adjectives
examples: This is the highest mountain here.
It is the oldest tree in the forest.

patterns.label: Block 5 · Superlatives · long adjectives
examples: This is the most beautiful valley.
That is the most popular walking route.

patterns.label: Block 6 · Should for advice
examples: You should take a map.
You should wear comfortable shoes.

patterns.label: Block 7 · Shouldn't for advice
examples: You shouldn't walk alone at night.
You shouldn't feed the wild animals.

patterns.label: Block 8 · Must for rules
examples: You must stay on the path.
You must take your rubbish with you.

patterns.label: Block 9 · Mustn't for prohibitions
examples: You mustn't light fires here.
Visitors mustn't swim in this lake.

patterns.label: Block 10 · Can for activities
examples: You can go cycling near the river.
You can see deer in the forest.

content.passage: The Green Valley Nature Park is a wonderful place for a day outdoors. It has a wide river, a deep lake and some of the highest hills in the county. The forest is quieter than the beach, and many visitors come here to watch birds and other wildlife. You can go hiking or cycling, but you must stay on the marked paths. The blue route is shorter than the red route, but the red route is more beautiful. You should wear comfortable shoes and take water with you. You mustn't feed the animals or leave rubbish in the park. In summer, the lake is the most popular place because visitors can sit by the water and enjoy the view.

content.audioTranscript: Welcome to Pinewood Nature Reserve. Today, the weather is sunny and the paths are dry. The green route is the shortest walk and takes about thirty minutes. The red route is longer, but it has the best views of the valley. You should wear comfortable shoes and take a bottle of water. Please stay on the paths because some plants are very rare. You mustn't feed the deer or leave any rubbish. You can stop for a picnic near the lake, but please take all your rubbish home. The visitor centre is beside the main car park. Enjoy your walk.
